guideTitle: Best EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 Solar Generators (2026)
metaTitle: Best EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 Solar Generators
metaDescription: Seven EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 and comparable power stations compared by capacity, 240V output, expansion, solar input and noise, for home backup.
expertTake: If you want one EcoFlow to run a house through an outage, buy the DELTA Pro 3: 4,096 watt-hours, 120 and 240 volt output, and room to expand to 48 kilowatt-hours. The older DELTA Pro is the value pick for 120 volt households, and the DELTA 3 Ultra is the quiet pick for essentials. Buyers with real whole-house loads should look at the DELTA Pro Ultra family, and anyone who only wants to run a CPAP, a laptop and a router should skip all of these and buy the small DELTA 3.
introParagraphs: A solar generator is a large battery, an inverter and a solar charge controller in one box, sold as a quiet, fume-free alternative to a gasoline generator. The label on the box states a capacity and a power rating, but the two numbers answer different questions, and mixing them up is the most common way buyers end up with a unit that cannot run what they own.

This guide explains how the DELTA Pro family and its siblings differ in capacity, output voltage and expansion, and how to match a configuration to your loads and your solar plan. The quick picks are above, and the model reviews below explain who each version suits and who should look at a different class.

products.name: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 4,096Wh 4,000W Power Station
products.description:
The DELTA Pro 3 is the current flagship of the DELTA Pro family and the machine most buyers searching this keyword actually want. It pairs a 4,096 watt-hour lithium iron phosphate battery with a 4,000 watt inverter that delivers both 120 volt and 240 volt output, so a well pump, a dryer or an electric range circuit is within reach in a way that a 120 volt-only station is not. Capacity is expandable to 48 kilowatt-hours with extra batteries or a smart generator, and EcoFlow's own framing is two to four days of whole-home essentials, which is a fair estimate only if you choose circuits carefully.

The feature that matters most in daily use is noise. X-Quiet cooling brings the unit down to about 30 dB at light load, which means it can sit in a bedroom or garage corner without announcing itself, and that is the reason to pick it over a gas generator. The 10 millisecond switchover works as a UPS for a NAS, server or desktop. The X-Boost mode lifts output to 6,000 watts for resistive loads such as a heater or a kettle by delivering less than full voltage, which is useful but does not help motors or electronics. Against the older DELTA Pro, you get more capacity and output from a similar-sized chassis.

Ownership is mostly about charging logistics. It will take solar, a wall outlet, a car input or the EcoFlow smart generator, so plan which combination you will use before buying panels, and check the solar input limits against your array voltage. The unit is a large, heavy device; it is portable by wheels, not by hand. The IP65-rated battery pack and automotive-grade LFP cells are a reasonable durability story, but a station this size should be placed on a dry floor, kept away from direct sun and given airflow. Bundles with a 400 watt panel, two 400 watt panels, or extra batteries are the same core unit with accessories added.
products.bestFor: Whole-home essential-load backup with 240V appliances and room to expand later.
pros: 4,096Wh battery and 4,000W inverter run 120V and 240V loads
Expandable to 48kWh with extra batteries or a smart generator
Quiet X-Quiet cooling, as low as 30 dB at light load
10 ms switchover works as a UPS for a NAS or computers
cons: Large and heavy, so it moves on wheels rather than by hand
X-Boost 6,000W is for resistive loads only, not motors or electronics

products.name: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3,600Wh 3,600W Power Station
products.description:
The original DELTA Pro is the unit that established this family and it remains a sensible buy while stock lasts. A 3,600 watt-hour LFP pack feeds a 3,600 watt inverter, and EcoFlow lets you pair two units to reach 7,200 watts and expand storage up to 25 kilowatt-hours with extra batteries or the smart generator. It supports five charging methods, including an electric-vehicle charging station and the car outlet, and the app shows each input and output in real time.

The key comparison is with the DELTA Pro 3. The newer unit has about 14 percent more battery at 4,096 watt-hours, a 4,000 watt inverter against 3,600 watts, 240 volt output built in and a much larger 48 kilowatt-hour expansion ceiling against 25. That means the older model is the economical choice if your loads are mostly 120 volt and sub-3,600 watts, but a poor choice if you want a 240 volt well pump or a larger future battery bank. Fast-charge claims are strong: 1.8 hours from a 240 volt outlet at 3,000 watts, 2.7 hours from a 1,800 watt wall outlet, and about 2.8 hours from four 400 watt panels.

Because it is the older platform, check accessory and extra-battery compatibility before buying, particularly if you plan to add the smart generator. The bundle with a 400 watt panel or two 220 watt panels is just the same station with solar, so compare panel wattage against the unit's input limits. Treat any older stock like any large battery: inspect the cord, keep it ventilated and avoid leaving it in a hot vehicle.
products.bestFor: Buyers with 120V essential loads who want a proven 3.6kWh station.
pros: 3,600Wh and 3,600W cover most refrigerator, sump and tool loads
Two units pair for 7,200W, and storage grows to 25kWh
Five charging options include 240V wall and EV stations
Fast 1.8 hr full charge from a 240V outlet is stated
cons: Smaller 25kWh expansion ceiling than the DELTA Pro 3
Older platform, so check accessory and battery compatibility first

products.name: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra 3,072Wh 3,600W Power Station
products.description:
The DELTA 3 Ultra is the smaller, quieter and more compact step down from the DELTA Pro 3, and it is the one to look at if essential-load backup, not whole-home reach, is the goal. A 3,072 watt-hour LFP battery feeds a 3,600 watt inverter with a 7,200 watt surge capability, which is enough for a refrigerator, a microwave, a modem and lights at once. EcoFlow states a 25 dB noise level under load, the quietest claim in this roundup, thanks to the X-Quiet 3.0 cooling design, and a switchover of less than 10 milliseconds protects computers and networking gear.

Compared with the DELTA Pro 3, you give up about a quarter of the battery capacity, the 240 volt dual-voltage output and the very large 48 kilowatt-hour expansion path. In return you get a lighter, simpler unit that costs less and matches the inverter wattage of the older DELTA Pro at 3,600 watts. Four charging options are listed, and EcoFlow's X-Stream tech speeds recharging from a wall outlet or solar. For an apartment, a small home or an RV, 3 kWh is a practical size.

Plan the install the same way as any station: place it on a hard, dry surface, give it room to breathe, and match any panels to its input rating. It is the right pick for people who need the 3,600 watt output and silence but not 240 volt appliances. Note that panels and the station often ship in separate packages in bundle listings.
products.bestFor: Apartments, small homes and RVs that want 3,600W output in a quiet package.
pros: 3,600W inverter with 7,200W surge handles fridge and microwave
Stated 25 dB under load is the quietest claim here
Under 10 ms UPS switchover protects PCs and networking
Four charging routes include wall, solar, car and smart generator
cons: No 240V dual-voltage output like the DELTA Pro 3
About a quarter less battery than the DELTA Pro 3

products.name: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max 2,048Wh 2,400W Power Station
products.description:
The DELTA 3 Max sits in the middle of the DELTA 3 family and is built around rapid recharging. EcoFlow states a 0 to 80 percent charge in about 1.13 hours, so you can bounce back between outages or between a night of use and the next day. A 2,048 watt-hour LFP battery with a 2,400 watt inverter and a 3,400 watt X-Boost mode runs a fridge, a modem and a few appliances for hours, and the X-Boost mode lets resistive loads like a space heater or a kettle exceed the nominal rating.

It makes the most sense as a one-room essentials unit or a camping and RV station rather than a home-backup anchor. Compared with the DELTA 3 Ultra, you give up 1,000 watt-hours and 1,200 watts of inverter, and the portability improves. Next to the DELTA 3 Classic at 1,024 watt-hours and 1,800 watts, it doubles the energy. It does not provide 240 volt output, so a dryer or well pump is outside its range.

The usual advice applies: the nameplate watt-hours are not usable watt-hours, because inverter and conversion losses mean you should plan on roughly 85 percent of the rating. Update the firmware and use the app's energy settings to prioritize loads. The solar panel is a separate purchase in some listings.
products.bestFor: Camping, RV and single-room backup where fast recharge matters.
pros: Stated 0 to 80% in about 1.13 hours recharges quickly between uses
2,400W inverter plus 3,400W X-Boost covers resistive loads
10 ms switchover and 10-year LFP design suit daily use
Doubles the energy of the DELTA 3 Classic for modest weight gain
cons: No 240V output, so well pumps and dryers are out of range
Too small to be the anchor of a whole-home backup plan

products.name: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra 6,144Wh 7,200W Home Battery System
products.description:
The DELTA Pro Ultra is where the family stops being a portable station and becomes a modular home battery. One kit includes an inverter and a 6,144 watt-hour battery, with a 7,200 watt, split-phase 120 and 240 volt output that can drive a central air conditioner or a well pump, and you can add batteries up to 15 in total for 90 kilowatt-hours. EcoFlow lists it as certified to both UL1973 and UL9540, which matters when an electrician or insurer asks about a home battery.

It behaves differently from the DELTA Pro 3. The app can prioritize circuits and shift loads against time-of-use rates, and a 20 millisecond switchover gives UPS-like protection for most electronics, though it is slower than the 10 millisecond rating on the portable units. A full charge in about 2 hours is a strength. The cost is size, weight and installation complexity: this is not something you carry to a campsite, and a transfer arrangement or smart home panel is part of the design.

If you are choosing between this and the DELTA Pro 3, think about where it lives. The Pro 3 is a movable station you can wheel out; the Pro Ultra is a semi-fixed system with an installation plan. Check local code and electrical permit requirements before connecting a home battery, and use a licensed electrician for any panel work.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want a modular, certified whole-house backup that can grow.
pros: 7,200W split-phase output handles central air and well pumps
Modular battery stack scales from 6kWh to 90kWh
Certified to UL1973 and UL9540 for home-battery use
Full recharge in about 2 hours per the listing
cons: Semi-fixed and heavy, with a transfer arrangement for the home
20 ms switchover is slower than the 10 ms portable units

products.name: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X 12,288Wh Home Power System
products.description:
This is the top of the family: a 12,288 watt-hour system, with output stated at 12 to 36 kilowatts and expansion up to 180 kilowatt-hours. It automatically switches between solar, battery and off-peak grid power to cut energy bills, and it restores power in under 20 milliseconds when the grid fails. That is whole-home territory, intended for homes with air conditioning, an electric vehicle charger and a lot of circuits.

The positioning is simple: if the DELTA Pro 3 is a very large power station, the Pro Ultra X is a home energy system. Next to the 6,144 watt-hour DELTA Pro Ultra, it doubles the energy in the base kit and sharply raises the output ceiling. It is the choice when you want to protect most of a house, not a handful of circuits. You can unplug it and take it when you move, with no hardwiring required, which separates it from a fixed whole-house battery.

The flip side is cost, weight and complexity, and the listing notes that the inverter and the extra battery are dispatched in separate packages. Plan placement, a transfer solution and an installer. For most people reading a keyword about a DELTA Pro solar generator, the DELTA Pro 3 is enough; this model is for homes with real daily loads and a budget to match.
products.bestFor: Large homes that want to run central air, an EV charger and most circuits from one system.
pros: 12,288Wh base kit with 12 to 36kW output covers most circuits
Expands up to 180kWh for long outages or daily solar shifting
Automatically switches between solar, battery and off-peak grid
Unplug and move with no hardwiring when you relocate
cons: Premium cost and weight far above a portable station
Inverter and battery ship separately, with real planning needed

products.name: EcoFlow DELTA 3 1,024Wh 1,800W Power Station
products.description:
The DELTA 3, sometimes sold as the DELTA 3 Classic, is the small door into the ecosystem. A 1,024 watt-hour battery and 1,800 watt inverter handle a CPAP, laptops, a router, a mini fridge and lights, and X-Boost supports resistive loads above 2,600 watts. EcoFlow states a full charge in 56 minutes when you combine 500 watts of solar with 1,500 watts of AC input, and an 80 percent charge in 30 minutes, which is quick for the class.

What makes it relevant to a DELTA Pro search is the expansion story. The DELTA 3 series can use DELTA 3, DELTA Pro 3 and DELTA 2 Max battery packs for up to 5 kilowatt-hours, so a small purchase can grow. LFP cells are rated for 4,000 cycles to 80 percent, which EcoFlow translates to ten years of daily use. It is the right pick for someone who does not need 240 volt output or a big fridge-and-freezer plan and who values portability.

Be realistic about the energy: a 1 kilowatt-hour unit keeps a modern fridge going for most of a day, not a week. Treat the ratings as nominal and expect roughly 85 percent of the battery to be usable. A 5-year customer service period is listed, so register it after purchase.
products.bestFor: Beginners, apartment dwellers and campers who want a fast-charging 1kWh station.
pros: 1,800W inverter with X-Boost handles heaters and kettles
Full charge in 56 minutes with solar and AC combined
Expands up to 5kWh with DELTA 3, Pro 3 or 2 Max packs
LFP cells are rated for 4,000 cycles to 80% capacity
cons: 1,024Wh runs a fridge for about a day, not through long outages
No 240V output and no whole-home capability

buyingCriteria.explanation: Watt-hours measure stored energy and watts measure how fast you can draw it. The DELTA Pro 3 stores 4,096 watt-hours and delivers 4,000 watts, so at full output it would drain in a little over an hour, while a 600 watt refrigerator cycle would stretch the same battery across a full day. Buyers often compare only the capacity and forget the inverter, and the reverse mistake is to buy high wattage and too little energy. Add up the running watts of the loads you actually need and size the battery for the hours you need, with at least 15 percent for conversion losses.

A 120 volt unit cannot run most well pumps, electric dryers, central air conditioners or EV chargers. The DELTA Pro 3, the DELTA Pro Ultra and the Ultra X provide 120 and 240 volt output, while the DELTA 3 Ultra, DELTA 3 Max, DELTA 3 and the original DELTA Pro are 120 volt-focused, though the DELTA Pro can pair two units. If a single 240 volt appliance is on your must-run list, that decides the class before capacity does.

Motors draw several times their running power when they start, and a refrigerator compressor or a well pump can pull a surge for a second or two. The DELTA 3 Ultra lists 3,600 watts continuous and 7,200 watts surge, and the DELTA Pro 3 lists 4,000 watts with X-Boost reaching 6,000 watts. X-Boost helps resistive loads like heaters and kettles by lowering delivered voltage, but it does not help motors or electronics. Check the starting watts of your largest motor and choose a unit with headroom, not just nameplate wattage.

Solar input sets how quickly panels refill the battery, and it has voltage and current limits. The original DELTA Pro states about 2.8 hours to charge from four 400 watt panels, but that is an ideal figure. In practice panels in winter or shade produce far less, so plan on a fraction of nameplate. Series versus parallel wiring changes voltage, and a mismatch can limit input, so check the input window before buying panels, especially when mixing bundles.

A station that cannot expand caps your storage forever. The DELTA Pro 3 expands to 48 kilowatt-hours, the original DELTA Pro to 25, the DELTA 3 series to 5 using compatible packs, and the DELTA Pro Ultra to 90 and the Ultra X to 180. The mistake is to buy a smaller unit planning to add later without checking that extra batteries are still sold and compatible. Within a family, batteries are not always interchangeable between generations.

A plug-and-play station runs loads through its own outlets, which needs no electrician. Backing up an entire panel is different: a transfer switch or a smart home panel and sometimes a permit are required. Never back-feed a home panel through a dryer outlet or a cable with two male ends, because that is dangerous to utility workers. The DELTA Pro Ultra line is certified to home-battery standards, while the portable units are designed to be plugged in directly.

specDecoder.meaning: The stored energy in the battery, measured in watt-hours. A 4,096Wh battery can supply 4,096 watts for one hour or 100 watts for about 40 hours before losses.
specDecoder.watchFor: Nameplate Wh is not fully usable. Expect about 85 percent after conversion losses, and less in cold weather.

specDecoder.meaning: Continuous watts is the sustained rating of the inverter, and surge is a brief peak for motor starts.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 7,200W surge on the DELTA 3 Ultra applies to starting loads for moments. It is not a promise to run 7,200 watts.

specDecoder.meaning: An EcoFlow mode that supplies resistive loads above rated watts by lowering the output voltage.
specDecoder.watchFor: It does not suit motors, compressors or electronics. A heater or kettle may run, while a refrigerator will not benefit.

specDecoder.meaning: The number of full charge and discharge cycles before capacity falls to a stated percent, usually 80 percent.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DELTA 3 states 4,000 cycles to 80 percent. Daily use shortens years faster than occasional backup use.

specDecoder.meaning: The delay between a grid failure and the battery taking over, shown as UPS or switchover time.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 10 ms units suit computers, but the 20 ms DELTA Pro Ultra family may reset some sensitive devices.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity, output and voltage
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked the lineup by energy stored and by output voltage, because those two figures set the class of loads each unit can serve. The DELTA Pro 3 at 4,096Wh and 4,000W and the Pro Ultra at 6,144Wh and 7,200W sit at the top, with the DELTA 3 at 1,024Wh at the bottom.

howWeEvaluated.title: Expansion and ecosystem
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how far each unit can grow, from the 5kWh ceiling of the DELTA 3 to 48kWh on the DELTA Pro 3, 90kWh on the Pro Ultra and 180kWh on the Ultra X. A higher ceiling and current-generation battery support scored higher, and older platforms were marked for compatibility checks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging speed and inputs
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated stated recharge times and input options: 1.8 hours at 240V for the original DELTA Pro, 0 to 80 percent in about 1.13 hours for the DELTA 3 Max and 56 minutes for the DELTA 3. We treated all as best-case, and rewarded units that accept wall, solar, car and generator inputs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and daily livability
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on spec sheets and owner feedback patterns, we compared noise claims of 25 dB for the DELTA 3 Ultra and as low as 30 dB for the DELTA Pro 3, and whether a unit can sit indoors. Quiet operation counts heavily for bedroom and apartment use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety, certification and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at battery chemistry, cell design, UPS transfer times and certifications such as UL1973 and UL9540 on the Pro Ultra. We also considered whether installation needs an electrician, since that changes who a unit suits more than its raw numbers.

howToChoose.subheading: Portable Station vs Home Battery System

cards.label: Portable station
cards.text: A single movable unit with its own outlets, such as the DELTA Pro 3, original DELTA Pro, DELTA 3 Ultra, DELTA 3 Max and DELTA 3. No electrician is needed to run loads from its sockets, and it moves with you. Capacity is fixed unless you add compatible packs.

cards.label: Home battery system
cards.text: A modular inverter and battery stack, as with the DELTA Pro Ultra and Ultra X, built for panel integration and large output. It scales to 90 or 180 kilowatt-hours, carries home-battery certifications and benefits from a transfer solution, but it is heavier and needs planning.

howToChoose.note: Choose a portable station if you want plug-in backup you can also use outdoors. Choose a home system if you want to power central air and a whole panel.

rows: 2.8 hours from four 400W panels, best case

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Home backup needs 240V output if you have a well pump or dryer, enough watt-hours for the circuits you choose and a safe connection method such as a transfer switch or smart panel. Quiet running helps if it sits indoors.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 is the best all-round portable choice, and the DELTA Pro Ultra is the best certified home-battery option. The DELTA 3 Ultra is the better pick if you only need 120V and silence.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need 240V loads, want to expand to dozens of kilowatt-hours or plan to power central air. Then the DELTA Pro 3, DELTA Pro Ultra or Ultra X justify the cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need a fridge, router and some lights. The DELTA 3 Ultra or DELTA 3 Max handles that, and the original DELTA Pro is a value pick for 120V households.

maintenance.task: Recharge to 40 to 60 percent for storage
maintenance.why: LFP cells age slowly when idle, but a long deep discharge can strain them. A partial charge keeps the unit ready.
Loose or heat-marked connectors waste power. Inspect AC cords and solar leads for wear.
Blocked vents raise temperatures and trigger fan noise or derating. Leave space on all sides.
Updates refine charge control and protections. Do it on a calm day, not mid-outage.
A battery that is never used hides faults. Run a real load for an hour to confirm output.
Dust and shade reduce solar input. Clean panels and check the wiring.

faq.q: Is the DELTA Pro 3 better than the original DELTA Pro?
faq.a: For most buyers, yes. It has more battery at 4,096 watt-hours against 3,600, a 4,000 watt inverter with 240 volt output and expansion to 48 kilowatt-hours. The original is still reasonable for 120 volt-only households that do not need that headroom.

faq.q: How long will a DELTA Pro run my refrigerator?
faq.a: A modern refrigerator averages a few hundred watt-hours a day, so a 3,600 or 4,096 watt-hour battery can cover it for several days if nothing else is running. Real time depends on the compressor's duty cycle, door openings and temperature. Use a plug-in watt meter to measure your fridge before you plan.

faq.q: Can I run a well pump or dryer on it?
faq.a: Only on a 240 volt unit. The DELTA Pro 3, DELTA Pro Ultra and Ultra X offer 240 volt output, while the DELTA 3 series and the original DELTA Pro are 120 volt-focused. Check the pump's starting watts as well as running watts.

faq.q: How many solar panels do I need?
faq.a: The unit's solar input rating is the ceiling. The original DELTA Pro states about 2.8 hours with four 400 watt panels under ideal sun, and real days produce much less. Choose panels that match the input voltage window and plan on a fraction of nameplate output in winter or shade.

faq.q: Is a solar generator safer indoors than a gas generator?
faq.a: Yes, because it produces no exhaust and no carbon monoxide. It still needs ventilation, a stable surface and protection from heat, and lithium batteries should not be charged in a blocked space. That fume-free operation is the main safety advantage.

faq.q: Is it worth buying the bundle with solar panels?
faq.a: Bundles simplify compatibility because the panels are chosen to match the station's input. The listing notes that some units and panels ship in separate packages. If you already have panels, check their voltage and connectors before buying a station alone.
